title: Affine geometric external Cech cup comparison on cocycles
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ schemes [def-pc-scheme] with affine relative diagonals, and $F,G$ quasi-coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $U,V$ be finite affine open covers. Let $A,B$ be their natural scalar Cech complexes and $T=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_kB)$; the right Cech functors are [def-sc-picard-external-right-cech-models]. Let $\theta$ satisfy the specified front/back cochain coordinates [lem-sc-picard-right-cech-cup-construction]. There exist factor comparisons $\alpha_p:H^p(A)\cong H^p(\mathrm{picardScalarModel}(f,F))$ and $\beta_q:H^q(B)\cong H^q(\mathrm{picardScalarModel}(g,G))$, and product comparisons $b_n:H^n(P(G))\cong H^n(\mathrm{picardScalarModel}(\mathrm{pr}_1\circ f,F\boxtimes G))$ [lem-sc-picard-kunneth-resolution-model]. For every $p+q=n$, factor Cech cocycles $a,v$ and total cocycle $z$ with inclusion equal to the tensor summand inclusion of $a\otimes v$, applying inverse total extension homology, $H^n(\theta_G)$, $b_n$, and the fixed scalar-model comparison to $[z]$ and multiplying the resulting class by $(-1)^{pq}$ gives $\operatorname{externalCup}(\epsilon_F(\alpha_p[a]),\epsilon_G(\beta_q[v]))$ [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations], cast along $p+q=n$. No equivalence from a direct sum of tensor homology classes, no scalar tensor-total comparison, and no invertibility of the cup operation is asserted.

proof.text: Apply the affine diagonal criterion and finite nonempty intersection closure to the factor covers. Each product tuple intersection is the intersection of the two projection inverse images of the factor tuple intersections, hence affine over the affine base. The product opens cover by choosing a factor open containing each projected point. Identify tensor pullback with module pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints to obtain quasi-coherence, then use tensor quasi-coherence.

Choose the canonical scalar Cech equivalences in every degree. Compose the factor comparisons with the inverse fixed scalar-model equivalences, and include extension homology for the product comparison b. All three comparisons keep their canonical normalization.

Apply the signed canonical scalar Cech external cup theorem to the cochain map specified by theta. Extension homology naturality and the inverse factor comparisons cancel. This gives (-1)^(p*q) times the product comparison equal to externalCup, with degree cast p+q=n. No rescaling of the normalization predicates is needed; the direct caller absorbs the sign on its homology summands.

lean.statement:
theorem picardRightCechCup_cycle_comparison
    {k : Type w} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{w}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal f)] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal g)]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    {ι κ : Type w} [Finite ι] [Finite κ]
    (U : ι → X.Opens) (V : κ → Y.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) (hV : ∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j))
    (hUc : iSup U = ⊤) (hVc : iSup V = ⊤)
    (θ : picardRightTensorCechFunctor f g U V F ⟶
      picardRightProductCechFunctor f g U V F)
    (hθ : IsPicardRightCechCup f g U V F θ)
    (G : Y.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] :
    let A := (picardCechFunctor f U).obj F
    let B := (picardCechFunctor g V).obj G
    let T := HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor A B (curriedTensor (ModuleCat.{w} k))
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)
    ∃ (alpha : ∀ p : ℕ, A.homology p ≃ₗ[k] (picardScalarModel f F).homology (p : ℤ))
      (beta : ∀ q : ℕ, B.homology q ≃ₗ[k] (picardScalarModel g G).homology (q : ℤ))
      (b : ∀ n : ℕ,
        ((picardRightProductCechFunctor f g U V F).obj G).homology (n : ℤ) ≅
          (picardScalarModel (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
            (externalCupCoefficients f g F G)).homology (n : ℤ)),
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : {pq : ℕ × ℕ // pq.1 + pq.2 = n})
        (a : A.cycles i.val.1) (v : B.cycles i.val.2) (z : T.cycles n),
        T.iCycles n z =
          HomologicalComplex.ιMapBifunctor A B (curriedTensor (ModuleCat.{w} k))
            (ComplexShape.up ℕ) i.val.1 i.val.2 n i.property
              ((A.iCycles i.val.1 a) ⊗ₜ[k] (B.iCycles i.val.2 v)) →
        (-1 : ℤ) ^ (i.val.1 * i.val.2) •
          picardScalarModelEquiv (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
            (externalCupCoefficients f g F G) n
          ((b n).hom (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (θ.app G) (n : ℤ)
            ((T.extendHomologyIso ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat (j := n) rfl).inv
              (T.homologyπ n z)))) =
          cast (congrArg (fun d ↦ ↥(scalarCohomology (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)
            (externalCupCoefficients f g F G) d)) i.property)
            (externalCup f g F G i.val.1 i.val.2
              (picardScalarModelEquiv f F i.val.1 (alpha i.val.1 (A.homologyπ _ a)))
              (picardScalarModelEquiv g G i.val.2 (beta i.val.2 (B.homologyπ _ v))))

Each product tuple intersection is the intersection of the two projection inverse images of the factor tuple intersections, hence affine over the affine base. The product opens cover by choosing a factor open containing each projected point. Identify tensor pullback with module pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints to obtain quasi-coherence, then use tensor quasi-coherence.

Choose canonical scalar Cech equivalences eX, eY and eP in every degree. Define alpha and beta by composing eX and eY with the inverse fixed scalar-model equivalences. Define b by product extension homology, eP, and the inverse product scalar-model equivalence. These are explicit compositions of the chosen characterized comparisons, in a theorem proof.

Extract the natural-index cochain map c and theta=extendMap(c) from htheta. Apply natural-degree scalar external cup compatibility to eX,eY,eP and the supplied cycles. Extension-homology naturality followed by inverse cancellation identifies the integer-degree expression with this natural-degree expression. Cancel the fixed scalar-model equivalences and retain the supplied degree cast.
